engagement_title: Ironway Run Club spring season: rebuild the founder's hand drawn numbering as artwork the kit shop can cut, recover the club mark off a screen printed singlet, and turn last year's printed bib into a live per member run
vertical: Health, wellness and fitness, a volunteer run community road running club with a thirty eight member roster and its own spring race (Providence, Rhode Island)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post 'Recreate Sports Jersey Font from Reference Image (Vector SVG / EPS)' (cands/cand_46.json, db_i 823), which asks a freelancer to 'Vectorize and recreate a sports jersey font from a reference image, including both letters (A-Z) and numbers (0-9)', lists 'Matching style and proportions from the reference image / Clean vector artwork', names the use as 'Football/Soccer jersey printing, DTF/Flex/Flock production', and requires 'Consistent stroke widths and spacing'. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com post 'Graphic Designer for DTF T-Shirt Printing' (cands/cand_50.json), wanting one 'clean, polished, print-ready file' with 'Transparent background, clean edges suitable for direct film transfer' and 'the original editable source file'. Neither post names a client, so the club, its founder, its members and its race are invented here. ENRICHED to the commission that client actually needed: a glyph set alone is an atomic op, and the real post's own framing shows the set exists to serve a season, so the season is the job. The optional 'OTF/TTF font file (bonus)' is deliberately not asked for, because no font design or font file output exists on this connector. The post's 'must be original vector artwork and not derived from proprietary font files' is honoured by the source being the founder's own ink drawing, which is why the recovery must be faithful rather than replaced by a lookalike typeface.
client_one_liner: Del drew our numbering by hand in 1994 and that lettering is the club, our only surviving club mark is on a photo of an old singlet, and in April the kit goes to the press shop and every member needs a bib with their own name and number on it.
client_brief:
Ironway Run Club, spring season

We are a volunteer run community club in Providence with thirty eight members on the books. Membership is forty dollars a season and covers everything, so what we print has to be cheap at volume and survive a wet April.

Two things land in the same month. Our new kit goes to the heat transfer shop, and we put on the Founders Five, our own road race, where every member runs with a bib.

The numbering. Del, who started the club in 1994, drew a full sheet of numerals and letters in ink, and that lettering is the club as far as our members are concerned. We still have his sheet and we photographed it. We need it turned into artwork the kit shop can cut and press: the ten numerals and the full alphabet as one set, one colour, plus a page showing exactly where a number sits on the back of a singlet and how big.

The mark. Our club mark only exists on a screen printed singlet from a few seasons back, which we photographed. There is no file anywhere and nobody knows who made it. We need it back as artwork we can put on the kit and on the top of every bib, and it has to still be our mark.

The bibs. Last year's printer sent the bib file back and we kept it. We want the same bib, personalised: each member's name, assigned number, pace group and emergency contact, one page per member, in the order our roster is in, so the volunteer sorting them at packet pickup can count down the list. One file the printer can run, and a separate file per member for the people who ask us to re-send theirs.

Our members are twenty two to sixty eight and half of them pin the bib on in the dark. Legible beats clever. And write us a note on what you did, and on anything the old file will not let us do.
price_band_and_audience: A forty dollar per season volunteer club, roughly thirty eight members, no sponsor. The band is load bearing in both directions. Downward it dictates one colour throughout: a single ink on the bib stock, a single cut colour on the heat transfer, numerals heavy enough to read from a marshal's distance in poor light, and no element that adds a plate or a pass. Upward it rules out the paid entry race look an agent drifts into by habit, which is a multi colour bib with a sponsor band, a timing chip zone, a tear off stub and a photo tag block, all of which cost money this club does not have. The founder's hand is the entire brand, so the treatment is reduced by necessity rather than by taste. Ship a premium event look and every technical gate can still pass while the commission is wrong. A posted job of this shape runs 400 to 900 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Volunteer run community road running club with its own spring race, printing kit and race bibs for its members.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1994 by Del in Providence, Rhode Island. A volunteer run club with roughly thirty eight members on the books.
brand_identity.about: Ironway Run Club is a volunteer community running club in Providence with about thirty eight members. Its identity is the numbering the founder drew by hand in 1994, which the members treat as the club itself, and a screen printed club mark that survives on an old singlet. Each spring the kit goes to the heat transfer shop and every member runs the club's own Founders Five race with a bib.
brand_identity.audience: Members aged roughly 22 to 68, half of whom pin a bib on in the dark before a wet April race. Volunteers, not customers.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A forty dollar per season volunteer club with no sponsor. Everything printed must be cheap at volume and survive weather: one colour throughout, nothing that adds a plate or a pass, and nothing that looks like a paid entry event.
brand_identity.typography: The founder's hand drawn numerals and alphabet are the display face and the whole brand. A plain, sturdy sans handles member names and directory copy where legibility at a marshal's distance matters more than character.
brand_identity.voice: Friendly, plain, volunteer to volunteer. A line the club would write: "Founders Five is on. Pin your bib, mind the puddles, we will see you at the line."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No digital brand files exist. The numbering survives only as a phone photograph of the founder's original ink sheet on drafting paper, and the club mark only as a photograph of it screen printed on an old singlet. Nobody knows who made the mark and there is no file of either. Last year's bib survives as the printer's returned press PDF.
brand_identity.values: The founder's hand is the club, so it is kept faithfully. Legible beats clever, and every member gets the same thing for their forty dollars.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_numbering_sheet.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: A phone photograph of the founder's original ink style sheet: numerals and the full alphabet drawn by hand on gridded drafting paper, lying on a table under a window.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Del's sheet. This is the lettering everybody in the club knows."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The sheet is a field of many disjoint strokes rather than one coherent mark, so a single selection returns a plausible looking mask that silently omits whole glyphs, and the printed grid sits close to the ink in value across the lower third where the founder pressed lighter. It also carries eleven numeral forms for ten numerals, an open top four and a closed top four side by side with nothing saying which is current, and the top two rows were drawn with a heavier nib, which is invisible on a sheet where every glyph is a different size.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_singlet_mark.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the club mark screen printed on an old singlet laid flat: a chevron and rail device inside a ring of small caps type, one ink on a mid tone jersey.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only place our mark still lives. Screen printed, a few seasons old, slightly faded."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The knit breaks the printed edge into a sawtooth the trace records faithfully, and it is a compound lockup, so a prompt naming the badge returns the type ring and outer arc while quietly dropping the inner chevron. Naming the garment returns the singlet instead of the ink, background removal on the ring gives back a solid opaque disc, and the ink runs close to the jersey in value along the fold crossing the lower left.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_bib_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last season's bib artwork as the printer returned it: a genuine press PDF at the club's bib trim, one ink, with the club mark placed as an image at the head of the page.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The bib we ran last year. The printer sent the file back and we kept it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the printed page shows and what the file is made of are different things, and the second is knowable only after conversion: the four blocks the eye reads as separate do not correspond to four editable frames, and the readout that describes the document's text is not the text the document holds. It also carries no bleed, and none can be introduced through this route.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_roster.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The membership roster as the secretary keeps it: member name, assigned number, pace group, emergency contact name and phone, in the order the club wants the bibs stacked.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Thirty eight rows, in the order we want them stacked at packet pickup."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two members hold the same number after a returning member rejoined, one row has an empty number cell, and the name column runs from six characters to a thirty one character double barrelled surname, none of which the secretary has noticed. A record whose name exceeds the space the artwork gives it does not push the layout or announce itself. It stops.

assets_supplied.name: ironway_kit_swatch.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A photograph of the new singlet fabric with the heat transfer shop's cut colour chip laid on it, so artwork is judged on the ground it will sit on.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The new kit colour and the transfer colour the shop stocks."

assets_supplied.name: ironway_kit_shop_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text from the heat transfer shop: back panel dimensions per singlet size, the number height the club has always used, the shop's minimum cuttable stroke at final size, and confirmation that they run one colour only.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the shop told us they need."

acceptance_bar: The press run is one file whose page count equals the reconciled roster count, in roster order, so the member on page N is the member on row N. Correct content in the wrong order is unusable at packet pickup and fails.

Every bib carries every field of its own roster row in full. A name stopping short of its last syllable, a missing pace group or an absent emergency contact fails the bib even though the page looks finished.
The numerals and letters read as one hand and one weight when the set is laid out at the size it actually prints on the kit.
Every counter in the set is still open at kit reproduction size on the club's own kit colour, judged on the swatch and never on white.
Exactly ten numerals and twenty six letters are delivered, one form each, and the choice made where the sheet offers more than one form is stated rather than made silently.
No stroke falls below the heat transfer shop's stated minimum at final size. Anything that does is named in the note rather than shipped.
The mark at the head of every bib is the recovered mark, not last season's placed scan, and the same mark appears on the apparel page and the spec sheet with no drift.
The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle underneath.
Per member files are named to the roster and the person named on the file is the person on the page. A set named by output position fails.
Proofs are genuinely at press resolution at trim, and no delivered file exceeds its source pixel dimensions.
The spec sheet and apparel page are one document the club can edit next season, with live retypeable text and the numbering as real vector shapes.
The note states what was applied and why, which numeral forms were chosen, how the roster was reconciled, and everything the old bib file will not permit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, where image_vectorize is counted rather than as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload and asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs, image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: All the archaeology. It levels and neutralises the founder's sheet, separates ink from printed grid where the two run close, lifts glyphs at stroke level rather than paper level, and traces them into a set. It repeats that recovery on the screen printed mark and splits the result into two forms for two destinations: a transparent scalable vector for the authored surfaces and a colour accurate raster plate for the frame inside the bib template, because the layout surface takes no vector. It also does the vector hygiene the tracer does not do for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout and variable data merge
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange, document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles and resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The bib run. Last season's press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the roster is bound to it, and the run is delivered twice off one merged document: a press file whose pages are the members in roster order, and per member single record files the club can re-send. Its interchange export is also the only honest inspection channel for what the converted document contains, which is what any defensible mapping rests on.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The apparel placement page and the numbering plus bib spec sheet as one native editable document at true physical canvases, the only surface here that composes free form layout. The numbering goes in as inline SVG so it stays real vector, the swatch and mark plate are inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, and each root declares its own canvas so a global override does not collapse them.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the spec sheet and apparel page, and the honest boundary of the commission. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on a plain club document rather than a sports brand. Numeric weights are non standard per family, every name must be laundered into canonical form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently. This surface also draws the line the note states: type control exists here and nowhere on the layout surface.

Persisting the numeral direction the two co-chairs actually sign off. Candidates go up as flattened proofs because vector is not accepted there, each call stays inside the twelve placement cap, and a partial success is read as partial rather than as done.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and decide which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: A per member run at volume is variable data work, a two canvas spec document is authored layout, the artwork is raster archaeology. The brief pins all three.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed tier that gates the export.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Handoff discipline, and it matters here because the same mark will exist in several forms and the manifest is what keeps them apart.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at the sheet, the singlet, the swatch and the shop note, straighten both captures before any crop is locked, and write a triage: where drawn stroke and printed grid run close, what the mark is made of, what the shop's minimum stroke means at the club's number height.
trajectory.judgement: The sheet is one photograph of many separate drawings and the count of glyphs on it is not the count the client needs. Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters plus a triage note covering ink against grid, glyph inventory and the shop constraint at print size.

trajectory.action: Neutralise the sheet and open the separation between drawn ink and printed grid, working the lower third with a confined correction rather than a whole frame move.
trajectory.judgement: A whole frame contrast move that clears the grid also thins the lightest strokes, which is the opposite of what the shop needs.
trajectory.produces: A prepared sheet master with the applied parameters logged.

trajectory.action: Lift the glyphs at stroke level with prompts naming the drawn line's own visual properties, take the returned bounds, invert polarity, and crop each group from its own bounds.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the paper pulls the selection to the substrate and every downstream trace becomes a rectangle. Polarity before tracing is the difference between a positive set and a black box with holes in it, and both routes report success.
trajectory.produces: Per group plates in correct polarity with each selection's returned bounds recorded.

trajectory.action: Trace the plates, inject a viewBox, remove the opaque full canvas path the tracer always writes first, and assemble ten numerals and twenty six letters as one set, deciding which of the two four forms is the club's.
trajectory.judgement: The tracer takes no options at all, so every quality lever lives upstream in the raster prep. The eleventh numeral form is a decision the client cannot make for the agent and has to be stated.
trajectory.produces: A hygienic glyph set as placeable scalable artwork, plus a stated choice for the duplicated form.

trajectory.action: Recover the club mark off the singlet: an ink level selection naming the printed device rather than the garment, correct polarity, a bounds crop, a trace with the same hygiene, and separately a colour accurate raster plate made by filling around the inverted mask at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Three calls the tools will not make: wording the selection so it takes ink and not jersey, judging whether the compound lockup came back whole or quietly partial, and deciding which produced form belongs on which surface. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A transparent scalable mark for the authored surfaces and a high resolution raster plate for the layout surface.

trajectory.action: Put the glyph set and the mark down at the sizes they actually reproduce, the number at the shop's stated height on the kit swatch and the mark at bib head size, and look at them there.
trajectory.judgement: Everything traced looks good at canvas scale. The only scale that means anything is the one the club prints at, on the ground it prints on, judged by eye rather than from any returned number.
trajectory.produces: Reproduction size proofs of the set and the mark on the real ground.

trajectory.action: Convert last season's bib PDF into a layout document, export its interchange form, and read what the conversion exposes: how many text frames exist, what each holds, where the placed mark sits.
trajectory.judgement: The printed page is evidence of a design, not of a file. The mapping strategy is decided by this readout and by nothing visible on the printed bib.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory naming the real text frames, their contents and the image frame carrying the mark.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping against the frames that exist, binding each roster field to a real frame identifier and the mark's frame to the recovered raster plate.
trajectory.judgement: Identifiers are integer item ids and not interchange strings, the mapping travels as one stringified object or parts of it are never seen, insert rows sharing a frame go in descending position order against the original text, and wholesale text replacement is rejected by validation, so targeted replacement is the workhorse.
trajectory.produces: A complete field mapping covering every roster column and the mark.

trajectory.action: Validate the mapping, prepare the merge template from it, then export the prepared template's interchange form and read it for every placeholder that was supposed to land.
trajectory.judgement: A validator reports on the shape of a mapping, not on a document, and preparation reports success either way. The only evidence that a field exists in the template is the field being visible in the template.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template and a placeholder by placeholder reading of what it contains.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster: settle the duplicated number and the empty number cell, fix the run order, and produce the file that will actually drive the merge.
trajectory.judgement: The club believes the roster is clean. Two members cannot wear one number at a road race and a bib with no number is not a bib, so this is a client facing decision, applied consistently and disclosed.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled run file and a written record of every change made to the club's data.

trajectory.action: Merge the reconciled roster into the template, then render off the merged document: the press file in roster order, per member single record files named to the roster, and proofs at press resolution at trim.
trajectory.judgement: Identity has to survive delivery, so the route is the ordered document or a single record loop, never files named by their position in a response. Resolution asked for at merge time is silently ignored.
trajectory.produces: One press file at roster length, a named per member set, and press resolution proofs.

trajectory.action: Look at the rendered bibs, going deliberately to the extremes of the roster rather than the first page: the longest name, the shortest, the reassigned number, the longest emergency contact.
trajectory.judgement: Page one is the page most likely to be fine. A run is verified at its extremes or it is not verified, and nothing in the merge response points at which record is extreme.
trajectory.produces: A read of the run at its extremes with any affected records named.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a forty dollar volunteer club document rather than a sports brand. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying two roots at their true physical sizes, the apparel placement page and the spec sheet, with the glyph set as inline SVG inside explicitly sized top left anchored wrappers, the swatch and mark plate inlined as image data, family and weight declared on every text element, then upload and export by URL after the readiness check.
trajectory.judgement: A right anchored auto sized wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, an image left as a URL is not an image, and a global canvas parameter collapses a two size document. The design work is how much room the number needs on a back panel and how plain the sheet should be at this tier.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML retained as the durable source, and a native editable document.

trajectory.action: Verify the export through both channels, resolving the rendition for the first canvas and parsing the returned markup for the second, then board the reconciled numeral candidates for the co-chairs and write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success without warning and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas. On the board, vector is not accepted and a partial success is not an error.
trajectory.produces: An inspected first canvas, a markup audit of the second, a persistent board with nothing dropped, and the written note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last season's bib actually is once it is a layout document, and whether the mapping built from the tool's own description of it survived into the template. Frame granularity from a converted PDF is not under anyone's control: blocks the eye reads as separate can arrive as one continuous story, so a per frame plan is not expressible and fields must be reached by position inside a single story. Worse, the readout the mapping was computed from is lossy in a way that leaves the text looking well formed, dropping a run while keeping its line break, so every position past the omission is short by the length of the dropped run. The validator returns valid with no warnings on those positions and the preparation step reports that placeholders were created successfully. Only the prepared template's own interchange form says which fields exist.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it: granularity is a property of how the printer built the file, and the omission sits inside the readout the tool exists to provide. An agent that already distrusts the readout and derives positions from the document itself simply passes this reading and continues, which is the right outcome for competence. (b) Nothing states it; the brief says only that the printer sent the file back. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different construction: positions recomputed against the true story, fields regrouped onto the frames that exist, insert rows re-ordered by descending position.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the document's own text rather than the tool's description of it, regroup the roster fields onto the frames that actually exist, re-prepare the template, and re-read its interchange form field by field before any merge is run.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A thirty eight page press run in which every bib is missing the pace group and the emergency contact, delivered with a success message at every step and a template the club re-runs next season with the same holes in it.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every member's bib carries that member's whole name. The name sits in a fixed measure frame inherited from last season's artwork, and text that exceeds it does not push the layout, does not wrap to a second line and does not raise an overset warning in the output. It stops. The page renders complete, the run reports success, and the only evidence is a surname ending mid word on the pages of members whose names are long. Which records are affected is a property of the club's actual names against a frame width that came from a file nobody measured, and cannot be known before the run exists.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not help and no parameter reflows a frame inherited from a converted document. (b) Nothing states it: the roster is presented as clean and the brief asks only that each member's name appear. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the fix is not another merge of the same data. Either the data changes under a house rule for shortening a name, applied across the whole roster and disclosed, or the field is re-bound so the surname carries its own line, and either way the run must be re-read at its extremes afterwards.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Identify every affected record by reading rendered pages rather than responses, decide and apply one consistent rule across the whole roster rather than patching individuals, re-merge, and re-read the extremes again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Several members collect a race bib with their surname cut in half, at a club run by volunteers where the bib is the only thing every member receives for their forty dollars.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the traced numbering holds where it is actually used. Traces of hand drawn ink are clean and convincing at canvas scale. At the shop's stated number height on the club's kit colour, the counters of the rounder glyphs can close into solid shapes, the sawtooth the trace inherited from paper fibre and jersey knit becomes a visible ragged edge, and the heavier nib the founder used on the first two rows reads as a different weight beside the rest of the set, which nothing on the sheet reveals because every glyph there is drawn at a different size. None of that is visible in the trace, in any returned value, or on the sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the information exists only once the set is at reproduction size on the real ground, and the tracer takes no options at all, so there is no parameter that could have been set correctly the first time. (b) Nothing states it: the brief calls the sheet the club's lettering and asks for artwork the shop can cut. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because every lever lives upstream in the raster preparation: a different confined correction before the lift, a differently worded stroke level selection, a re-trace, and the same judgement made again at size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the affected glyphs in the raster stage, re-lift and re-trace, normalise the set to one weight rather than accepting the sheet's two, and re-judge the whole set together at reproduction size on the swatch instead of glyph by glyph on white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A kit run where the club's own numerals print with filled counters and mismatched weights, unrecoverable after heat transfer, paid for out of a forty dollar per member season.

deliverables.name: Ironway numbering system and recovered club mark
deliverables.spec: Ten numerals and twenty six letters recovered from the founder's ink sheet as one weight normalised single colour set, plus the club mark recovered from a screen printed garment, all as placeable scalable artwork with a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas path underneath. The mark is delivered both as transparent scalable artwork for the authored surfaces and as a colour accurate raster plate at real resolution for the layout surface, because one form cannot serve both. Every stroke at or above the shop's stated minimum at final size, with exceptions named.

deliverables.name: Founders Five bib run, press file and per member set
deliverables.spec: Last season's press PDF reverse engineered into a live merge template carrying the recovered mark, bound to the reconciled roster and delivered twice off one merged document: a press file whose page count equals the reconciled roster count with pages in roster order, and per member single record files named to the roster with identity guaranteed rather than inferred from output position. Plus fabricator proofs at press resolution at trim.

deliverables.name: Apparel placement page and numbering plus bib spec sheet
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying two roots at their true physical sizes: the back panel placement page showing number height and position per singlet size, and the spec sheet covering the numbering, the mark and the bib. Live retypeable text in one licensed type system, the numbering present as real vector shapes rather than a picture of the set, the swatch and mark carried as embedded image data, delivered with the self contained source.

deliverables.name: Handover note and committee board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the parameters applied at each stage, which numeral form was chosen where the sheet offered two and why, every change made to the club's roster, the type system by role with family, foundry and actual numeric weight, any stroke that could not meet the shop's minimum, and what the old bib file structurally will not permit. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the numeral candidates the co-chairs sign off, with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press file's page count equals the reconciled roster count, and the reconciliation itself is written down.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the PDF page count and compare it against the row count of the reconciled run file named in the handover note.

verifiers_auto.text: The prepared merge template contains a live placeholder for every mapped roster field, not only the ones that happened to land.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the prepared template's interchange form, unzip it and search the story XML for each expected field token.

verifiers_auto.text: The per member set has one single page file per reconciled roster row, each named to its member.
verifiers_auto.how: Count the delivered files, assert each is one page, and diff the file names against the reconciled roster's name column.

verifiers_auto.text: The proofs are at press resolution at trim rather than a screen scale page.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the pixel dimensions against the bib trim and check the reported image density in the file headers.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered raster exceeds its source pixel dimensions and no captured tool response carries an upscale tradeoff entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare every delivered file against its source per the manifest and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the note's resize table.

verifiers_auto.text: Every delivered glyph and the mark carry a viewBox and no full canvas opaque path at index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse each delivered SVG, assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The authored export returned two roots, each keeping its own declared canvas size, with the numbering present as vector path shapes and no image resolved to the importer's placeholder.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide count and per slide dimensions from the export response, then parse the returned markup for path shape elements and for one by one placeholder image data.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed face, and the committee board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed items list.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node against the families the kit call returned, and read the board response's added and failed arrays.

verifiers_human.how: Set the full set at the shop's stated number height on the kit swatch and judge stroke weight, counter size and rhythm as a set.

verifiers_human.text: The counters are still open where the numbering actually prints, on the club's colour and not on white.
verifiers_human.how: View the set at final size against the swatch, looking at the rounder glyphs and at any glyph the note flags.

verifiers_human.text: The bib is legible in the conditions it will be used in, at a marshal's distance and in poor light.
verifiers_human.how: View a rendered bib at print size at distance and judge number height, contrast and surrounding space.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a forty dollar volunteer club, not a paid entry event with sponsors.
verifiers_human.how: Judge ink count, decoration, zoning and type register against the stated band and audience.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the club something they did not already know, including what could not be delivered and why.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and confirm every reconciliation, parameter and limit is named.

decision_gates: Which deliverable belongs on which surface, given that a per member run at volume, a two canvas authored document and raster archaeology are three different kinds of work.

Selection wording on the founder's sheet: naming the paper takes the substrate, naming the drawn line's own visual properties takes the ink, and the grid sits closest to the ink exactly where the drawing is lightest.
How to treat the eleventh numeral form, since the sheet offers two fours and the client has not noticed.
Whether to normalise the founder's two nib weights into one system or preserve the hand as drawn. Preserving it is defensible on a poster and indefensible on a numbering system.
Which form of the recovered mark goes where: scalable transparent artwork onto the authored surfaces, raster plate into the layout frame, never the reverse.
Whether the compound lockup came back whole, since a partial selection succeeds, looks plausible and is missing an element.
Whether the printed bib's visible blocks correspond to anything the converted document contains, which decides the whole mapping strategy.
How to reconcile a roster the client believes is clean, given a duplicated number and an empty number cell, and how to say so without embarrassing the secretary.
How to deliver identity safely for a per member run, since files named by their position in a response are not files named by who is on the page.
The type pairing for the spec sheet, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a volunteer club document rather than a sports brand.
How much the sheet says and how plainly. At this tier restraint is not a style choice, it is what the club can afford to print.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of race bibs and a plausible set of numerals. IDENTITY: the numbering is one specific person's hand from 1994 and the mark is this club's actual screen printed mark, so a regenerated set is a different club's lettering, which the members recognise instantly because that lettering is what they think the club looks like. SPEC: the run is thirty eight pages in the club's own roster order, each page carrying that member's real name, number, pace group and emergency contact, plus per member files named to real people, at press resolution at trim, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the merge template must be re-runnable next season with a new roster by the club's next volunteer, and the spec sheet must be retypeable. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the mark come back whole, do these counters survive at kit size, does every field actually exist in the template, does this member's name reach its last letter at trim.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces counted honestly with image_vectorize counted as imaging and no dead surface used. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with tradeoffs, fill_area and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, including ink level selection of a printed graphic off a photographed object (a 9,372 px stroke only mask with counters correctly excluded) and a full colour vector of a knockout plate preserving brand hues. INDESIGN: the whole convert, idml, mapping, prepare, merge, render chain is verified end to end, a bare press PDF was reverse engineered into a live template whose story contained every expected token, one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page count equal to row count, per record identity is guaranteed by createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop, and 300 dpi at trim comes from the render because the merge's own resolution parameter is silently ignored. The checkpoints rest on live findings: a six line flow converted to ONE text frame; the mapping readout dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break so every later offset was short, the validator still returned valid, prepare still reported success and only 3 of 5 mappings landed; and vectorize takes no options at all. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true physical canvases at 96 dpi, inline SVG becoming native editable vector and a genuine editable document are verified, the rendition preview is first canvas only, and photographs must be inlined as image data because every URL resolved to a placeholder. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, and the absence of any font file download is why the note must state that type control does not exist on the layout surface. BOARDS: persistence, the twelve placement cap, partial success at 201 and no vector are verified. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no generative call of any kind, no bleed claim on a converted template, no named press preset, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
